Q: What is brushed moleskin, and why is it such a good shout for tailoring?
A: Moleskin is a dense cotton fabric with a sheared and brushed surface, which gives it that soft, almost suede-like handle. It is hard-wearing, wind-resistant and a little more relaxed than traditional suiting cloth, meaning your blazer looks sharp without feeling overly polished.
Why wear it? Because it brings texture and depth to tailoring, especially in cooler months. It has a matte finish, a bit of substance, and enough structure to hold a proper tailored shape.
The Percival spin: Think of it as tailoring with better chat. Button it up with the matching trousers when the dress code says smart, or leave it open over a tee when you want to look sorted with minimal admin.

p-wythenewyork-8508028321923.d:
The Souvenir Jacket has earned it's place among vintage collectors for good reason, they are incredibly special pieces that had tons of sentimental value and each being unique to the original owner.
Post WWII, GIs would have these Souvenir Jackets made, often decorating their own flight jackets, with embroideries and patches that would represent places they traveled or different places they were stationed. From there, many different iterations took form, and the Souvenir Jackets evolved into a satin varsity-jacket-like creation with tons of beautiful embroideries.
The Southwest Souvenir Jacket is special to Wythe. Both sides (the jacket is reversible!) feature a chainstich-embroidered map of the American Southwest, places we've traveled and have made our own memories. The front of the outer side features two armadillos on the chest, while the reverse side shows off steer-heads, motifs both of which are also iconic to the southwest and to us.

• Smile pockets
• Chainstitch embroideries on both the face and reverse sides, front and back
• Quilted lining/reverse side
• 60% Acetone, 40% Tencel
• Made in Portugal
